stated: Reform UK will undertake a major simplification of the UK's tax code, citing its current complexity of over 21,000 pages.

source.quote: Reform the Tax System Major simplification is needed. At over 21,000 pages, the UK’s tax code is a burden. Hong Kong’s tax code is under 500 pages.

bearing_set.reason: Any major restructuring of the tax code directly affects households' disposable income and compliance costs — the direction is genuinely contested (simplification could remove reliefs that benefit lower earners, or reduce burdens that squeeze take-home pay), but the effect is non-negligible.

Reducing a 21,000-page tax code lowers compliance and administration costs for businesses and individuals, credibly boosting productivity, business investment and dynamism — all O13 indicators — regardless of which specific reliefs or rates are ultimately changed.

membership_note: The policy as stated addresses structural complexity, not rates or reliefs directly, so effects on O11 (take-home pay), O12 (fiscal sustainability) or O14 (inequality gap) depend entirely on unspecified implementation choices and cannot be directionally assessed at this stage. O13 via compliance-cost reduction is the one mechanistically clear, non-negligible bearing.
